For children under 5, stay at Choeng Mon: it is the calmest bay on Koh Samui, has a low-tide sandbar to the islet of Koh Fan Noi and is 5–10 minutes from the airport. Lipa Noi on the west coast has even shallower, calmer water that toddlers love, but it is 40–50 minutes from the airport and our east-side boat trips add 400 THB per person return for pickups there. North Chaweng is the pick if you want restaurants within walking distance. Avoid Bophut and Bang Rak if swimming matters: the water is shallow and often cloudy.

Our verdict: the three best family areas

  1. Choeng Mon for toddlers and young children: a sheltered 1 km bay with soft sand, a gentle slope and usually flat water, beach restaurants and the airport close by. Mid-range rooms cost about 3,000–7,000 THB a night. Quiet after dark.
  2. North Chaweng for families who want convenience: the gentlest stretch of Samui's main beach, quiet at night, with hundreds of restaurants, Central Samui mall and three private hospitals 5–10 minutes away. Red flags are common from October to December.
  3. Lipa Noi for babies and toddlers who just want to paddle: very shallow, warm water with a sandy bottom and few waves, plus west-coast sunsets. The trade-offs are distance, few restaurants and tidal flats at low tide.

Airport times are by car outside rush hour. Hospital times are our estimates by road to the nearest private hospital with a 24-hour emergency room; allow more in Chaweng's evening traffic. Where to stay by age

Babies and toddlers (0–4)

You want flat water you can stand in, shade, a short drive to a hospital and a kitchen or restaurant nearby. Choeng Mon ticks every box: the centre of the bay is the easiest for paddling, and the western end is rockier. Lipa Noi has the flattest water on the island and stays calm through the monsoon months because it faces west, but the sea retreats over sand flats at low tide, so time beach visits for mid to high tide and book a place with a pool for the rest of the day. Infants travel free on our boat trips, and the Pig Island speedboat is the easiest first outing: the crossing from Thong Krut takes 15–30 minutes.

Children aged 5–11

Children who can swim open up the whole east coast. North Chaweng gives you easy water from January to September and every kind of food on foot, which matters with fussy eaters. Chaweng Noi and Silver Beach suit confident swimmers who like snorkelling around rocks. This is the age when the island's activities work best: elephant sanctuaries, ziplines from 6, go-karts from 9, and the full-day Ang Thong trip by big boat (from 16 December). Child rates on our shared trips apply from 3 to 11.

Teenagers

Teens usually want something going on in the evening and a beach with real waves or a reef. Chaweng and Lamai are the best bases: walkable restaurants, markets, Muay Thai classes and, for older teens, the beach clubs in daylight hours. Lamai is cheaper and calmer at night than central Chaweng. From Chaweng it is also easy to join a Koh Tao snorkelling day or a Discover Scuba dive (PADI's minimum age is 10).

Most private pool villas on Samui do not have pool fences. If you travel with toddlers, ask the owner for a photo of the pool area, whether a removable fence or a pool alarm is available, and whether the pool has a shallow step. Also check the road: many hillside villas above Chaweng Noi, Bophut and Lamai sit on steep concrete lanes that are hard with a pushchair and dangerous on a scooter. Ask how far it is to the nearest shop. Browse Koh Samui villas by area and bedroom count.

Family hotel checklist

  • Beach access: is the hotel on a swimmable stretch, or across a road? Ask for a photo of the sea at low tide.
  • Pools: a shallow children's pool or a pool with a wide step; shade over part of it.
  • Rooms: connecting rooms or family suites, a cot on request, blackout curtains for naps and a fridge for milk.
  • Kids' club and babysitting: check ages, hours and whether there is a charge.
  • Food: a restaurant that opens early for children's meals and cooks without chilli on request.
  • Getting out: a 7-Eleven or pharmacy within walking distance, and an easy taxi or Grab pickup point.
  • Hills and steps: hillside resorts often have steep paths and many stairs, which are hard with a pushchair.

Season and sea safety by coast

  • East coast (Chaweng, Lamai, Chaweng Noi): best from January to September. From October to December the north-east monsoon brings big waves and rip currents, and red flags are common. Few beaches have lifeguards.
  • North-east (Choeng Mon): sheltered by headlands and often calmer than Chaweng in the monsoon, but red flags still go up in strong north-easterly winds.
  • North and west coasts (Maenam, Bophut, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam): calm for most of the year but tidal, with long flats at low tide. Check the tide before you plan a swim.
  • Jellyfish: box jellyfish are rare but present in Samui waters, more often in calm, warm water after rain. Avoid swimming at dusk, use netted areas where they exist, and pour vinegar on a sting for at least 30 seconds before calling 1669. Many hotels keep vinegar stations on the beach.

Healthcare near each family area

Bangkok Hospital Samui on the ring road near Chaweng Noi has a paediatric department and a 24-hour emergency room (+66 77 429 500, or 1719 from a Thai phone), which makes Chaweng, Chaweng Noi and Choeng Mon the best-placed areas for families with a child who has a medical condition. Samui International Hospital at the north end of Chaweng Beach Road and Bandon International in Bophut are closer to the north coast. On the west coast the nearest emergency room is the government Koh Samui Hospital near Nathon; for private care allow 35–45 minutes. Private hospitals ask for a deposit or an insurance guarantee, so carry your policy number. Ambulance: 1669. More on our hospitals page.

Day trips from your base

Wherever you stay, you can reach the best family boat day. The Pig Island and Koh Tan speedboat (1,450 THB, child 1,250 THB, 4–5 hours) runs every day of the year from Thong Krut. The Ang Thong big boat (1,500 THB, child 1,100 THB plus the cash park fee) suits children of about 6 and older, from 16 December to 31 October.
